Given specific heat of the water 4200 J kg-1 °C-1

Latent heat of the water =2260  kJ kg-1

questions.q: Two different wires having lengths <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and respective temperature coefficient of linear expansion <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo></math> are joined end-to-end. Then the effective temperature coefficient of linear expansion is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The wire are joined end-to-end, so they are in series combination, then total length of wire is given by
L=L1+L2  ...(1)

When the temperature is increase by ∆θ, then its final length is given by using concept of linear expansion,
L'=L(1+α∆θ)  ...(2)

Using equation (1) and (2) for the series combination of wires, final length is given by

L'=L1'+L2'  ...(3)

⇒L1+L2(1+αeff∆θ)=L1(1+α1∆θ)+L2(1+α2∆θ)

⇒αeff=L1α1+L2α2L1+L2

questions.q:
Heat energy of 184 kJ is given to ice of mass 600 g at -12 °C, Specific heat of ice is 2222.3 J kg–1 °C–1 and latent heat of ice is 336 kJ kg–1.

(A) Final temperature of system will be 0 °C

(B) Final temperature of the system will be greater than 0 °C

(C) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of 5 : 1

(D) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of  1 : 5

(E) The final system will have water only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

∆Q=184×103 J,

m=0.600 kg at -12 °C,

S=2222.3 J kg–1 °C–1 and

L=336×103J kg-1

Heat required to convert ice from –12 °C to ice at 0 °C will be, 

Q1=0.600×2222.3×12=16000.56 J

Remaining heat Q=184000-16000.56

= 167999.44 J

Heat required to melt ice completely at 0 °C,

Q2 = 0.600 × 336000 = 201600 J needed which is more than Q, so 100% ice is not melted.

For amount of melted ice, we can write

167999.44=m×336000⇒m= 0.4999 kg

∴ mass of water =0.4999 kg

Mass of ice remaining = 0.1001

∴ Ratio =0.10010.4999≈1:5

questions.q: The temperature of a body in air falls from $40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $24^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in 4 minutes. The temperature of the air is $16^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The temperature of the body in the next 4 minutes will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \Delta T=T_2-T_1=16^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\
& \text { And } T_0=16^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\
& \frac{\Delta T}{t_1}=-k\left(32-16^{\circ}\right)...(i) \\
& \frac{\left(24-T_3\right)}{4}=-k\left(\frac{24+T_3}{2}-16\right) ....(ii) \\
& \frac{16}{4}=-k(16) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\left(24-T_3\right)}{4}=-k\left(12+\frac{T_3}{2}-16\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{16}{24-T_3}=\frac{16}{T_3} T_2 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{T_3}{2}-4=24-T_3 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{3 T_3}{2}=28 \\
& \Rightarrow T_3=\frac{56}{3}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of iron nail is hit by a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> hammer striking at a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>ms</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. What will be the rise in the temperature of the nail if one fourth of energy of the hammer goes into heating the nail ? [Specific heat capacity of iron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>42</mn><msup><mi>Jg</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mo>∘</mo></mmultiscripts><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If we heat-up an object, then, the energy is used to either change the temperature of the body or to change the state of the body.
If it changes the temperature, then,

Q = mS∆T
where, Q is the heat given, m is the mass and ∆T is the change in temperature.

We know that a moving object has an energy in the form of kinetic energy, i.e.,
KE=12mv2

When that moving object strikes another object, it loses some energy which changes into the heat energy and this heat energy increases the temperature of the object.
Given a hammer of 1.5 kg is moving with 60 m s-1.
Kinetic energy =12mv2 = 12(1.5) (60)2 = 2700 J
One-fourth of kinetic energy changes into heat energy.
⇒   14(KE) = Heat energy
⇒   14(KE) = m(S)(∆T)
⇒   14(2700) =(100) (0.42) (∆T)
⇒   ∆T=16.07°C

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : When a rod lying freely is heated, no thermal stress is developed in it.

Reason R : On heating, the length of the rod increases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> are true and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is the correct explanation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>

Both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> are true but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is NOT the correct explanation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Thermal stress is mechanical stress created by any change in temperature of a material. When the body is under some constraints, thermal stress is generated. But if it is lying freely, no thermal stress is developed.

The increase in length of a body with temperature is given by

∆L=Lα∆T

So, with the increase in temperature, the length of the rod increases.

A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: Two conductors have the same resistances at 0 °C but their temperature coefficients of resistance are α1 and α2. The respective temperature coefficients for their series and parallel combinations are :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Change in resistance due to temperature is given by, R'=R1+α∆T

For Series Combination:

Req=R1+R2

⇒2R1+αeq∆T=R1+α1∆T+R1+α2∆T

⇒2R1+αeq∆T=2R+α1+α2R∆T

⇒αeq=α1+α22

For Parallel Combination:

1Req=1R1+1R2

⇒1R21+αeq∆T=1R1+α1∆T+1R1+α2∆T

⇒21+αeq∆T=11+α1∆T+11+α2∆T

⇒21+αeq∆T=1+α2∆T+1+α1∆T1+α1∆T1+α2∆T

⇒21+α1∆T1+α2∆T=2+α1+α2∆T1+αeq∆T

⇒21+α1∆T+α2∆T+α1α2∆T=2+2αeq∆T+α1+α2∆T+αeqα1+α2∆T2

Neglecting small terms

2+2α1+α2∆T=2+2αeq∆T+α1+α2∆T

⇒α1+α2∆T=2αeq∆T

⇒αeq=α1+α22

questions.q: A block of ice at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is slowly heated and converted to steam at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Which of the following curves represent the phenomenon qualitatively:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the state of the substance is not changing, temperature of the substance increases when heat is supplied to it. But when the substance changes the state, the heat supplied to it used as latent heat and the temperature remains constant until all the substance converts to other state.

Therefore, temperature of ice first increases from -10 °C to 0 °C. Then, remains constant at 0°C till whole ice is melted. Then, it increases from 0 °C to 100 °C. Again it remains constant at 100 °C till whole water converts into steam.

questions.q:
A geyser heats water flowing at a rate of 2.0 kg per minute from 30°C to 70°C. If geyser operates on a gas burner, the rate of combustion of fuel will be _____ g min-1.

Given here, mass flow rate of water, dmdt=2 kg min-1

The geyser heats the water, raising the temperature from θ1=30°C to θ2=70°C.

Total heat utilised in raising the temperature, ΔQΔt=dmdt×sΔθ

ΔQΔt=260×4.2×40=mt×L

L= heat of combination=8×103 J g-1

Now, rate of consumption of fuel is mt=2×4.2×4060×8×103

=4.26×10-3=0.7×10-3 kg sec-1

=42 g min-1

questions.q:
Two cylindrical rods A and B made of different materials, are joined in a straight line. The ratio of lengths, radii and thermal conductivities of these rods are :
$\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{B}}}=2$ and $\frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{1}{2}$. The free ends of rods A and B are maintained at $400 \mathrm{~K}, 200 \mathrm{~K}$, respectively. The temperature of rods interface is ________ K, when equilibrium is established.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}_1=\frac{\ell_1}{\mathrm{~K}_1 \mathrm{~A}_1}, \mathrm{R}_2=\frac{\ell_2}{\mathrm{~K}_2 \mathrm{~A}_2} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{dQ}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{dQ}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right)_1=\left(\frac{\mathrm{dQ}}{\mu}\right)_2 \\ & \frac{400-\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{R}_1}=\frac{\mathrm{T}-200}{\mathrm{R}_2} \\ & \frac{400-\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{T}-200}=\frac{\mathrm{R}_1}{\mathrm{R}_2}=\left(\frac{\ell_1}{\ell_2}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}_2}{\mathrm{r}_1}\right)^2 \times \frac{\mathrm{K}_2}{\mathrm{~K}_1} \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 \times 2 \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) \\ & \frac{400-\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{T}-200}=\frac{1}{4} \\ & 1600-4 \mathrm{~T}=\mathrm{T}-200 \\ & 5 \mathrm{~T}=1800 \\ & \mathrm{~T}=360 \mathrm{~K}\end{aligned}$
